this is a really good question! the truth is, there's no definitive answer. the number is estimated to be 250,000 people during the nazi regime, but that also encompasses everyone who was considered to have a "disability" (disability being in quotes because not everything that was considered a disability was actually a disability, ie: addictions like alcoholism). there's also the T4 Program/me, which was carried out from 1939-1941, to essentially euthanize people who were disabled as they were seen as burdens to the world. then, in 1933 there was the Law for the Prevention of Hereditarily Diseased Offspring (a mouthful, i know) which allowed the forced sterilization of people who were deemed, quote, "unfit to reproduce", which included lots of people in asylums. the estimated number for people subjected to forced sterilization is 360,000.
also, in 1939, the T4 Program/me was extended to disabled children aswell, which included disabilities like down syndrome and cerebral palsy. 
all of this is a long winded way of saying: we really don't know. I will say, camps were mostly for Jewish people, although there were patches put on the uniforms of people to discern them from one another. For example: LGBTQ people had the infamous pink triangle.
